reason: Directly on parser differentials for PDF forensics; the repair engine's multi-engine verification (GAP-012) and tamper indicators (GAP-015) can reuse its error-feature approach.
Real-world truncation prevalence and the origin of the issue-tracker (stressful) corpus; needed for charter 3(a) damage evidence.
Core LangSec PDF parsing/validation paper with real-world prevalence of incremental updates and syntax errors; normalization is a CDR-style rewrite whose evidence loss matters for GAP-016.
Primary evidence for DMG-009 attack templates and for GAP-015/GAP-016: revision-aware analysis is what detects them; repair that collapses revisions erases the evidence.
Real-world prevalence of cross-engine disagreement (GAP-012) and an automated multi-reader oracle design; explicitly frames file repair as future work.
Real-world non-compliance prevalence in crawled PDFs and the LangSec argument that divergent repairs are an attack surface.
Most promising real-world truncation source and natural-pair candidate for charter 3(a); pairs still need prefix verification.
Machine-readable spec from SafeDocs; relevant to the conformance oracle (charter §2) and to object-type inference during repair.
Formal model of xref/incremental-update resolution is exactly what xref reconstruction and revision choice need.
Verified/safer PDF parsing; a candidate reference parser for differential checks.
Earliest formal-verification attempt; source of the xref-loop ambiguity.
Attack templates for DMG-009 using malformed incremental updates.
More incremental-update attack templates (DMG-009); certification semantics for signature-preserving emission (GAP-016).
Hostile-input taxonomy for the repair engine's safety envelope (charter threat model).
Canonical parser-differential exploitation paper; templates for DMG-009 and motivation for GAP-012.
CDR rebuilds a clean PDF from a parsed model - the closest neighbour of repair emission; item 3 of this brief. Not read (read quota); first candidate for the next read.
Polyglot/junk-prefix inputs overlap with DMG-013; detection needed before repair.
Newer polyglot measurement; same relevance as SRC-0216.
Hostile real-world PDF source with per-tool error labels; a candidate adversarial corpus for DMG-009.
Normalization/rewriting of PDFs under a checker - CDR-style emission relevant to GAP-016 and GAP-103; may partly close GAP-103.
Grammar-based PDF validation.
Taxonomy of how parser differentials arise; supports tamper-indicator design (GAP-015).
Tooling for corpus-wide multi-parser behaviour analysis; candidate evaluation infrastructure (W3).
Likely source of per-parser failure rates on crawled PDFs (prevalence, GAP-105).
Same as SRC-0223; the bug-tracker (stressful) corpus is a real-world malformed-file source.
De facto vs de jure PDF: what engines actually accept is the repair target.
Background taxonomy for hostile-input handling in the repair parser.
Likely real-world prevalence of recoverable earlier revisions; sanitization is CDR's privacy side. Probably overlaps scoping-forensics.
Validator trust matters for choosing the conformance oracle (charter §2, GAP-106); the preservation community is a prevalence lead.
Directly on automated document (incl. PDF) repair from the software-engineering side; missing from the REPDF lineage.
Transferable learned-constraint repair method and an early output-quality metric.
Redaction side channel, not structure repair; left to scoping-forensics.
ML malware detection evasion; no parsing/repair content.
Malware detection of embedded JavaScript; not structure repair.
Malware-trace forensics magazine article; not about malformed structure or repair.
Another Common Crawl PDF corpus; may report how many crawled PDFs are truncated or unparseable. Found in the still-open check for GAP-100.
Newer cross-viewer inconsistency work; checked for GAP-102 (it targets document generators, not repair). Found in the still-open check.
Font-based content masking could be a DMG-009 template and matters to font repair; hand to scoping-fonts.
